site.name: BAPN
site.description: BAPN is Christchurch's badminton academy for juniors and adults — BWF-certified head coaches, a structured pathway from first racket to representative level, and recovery and nutrition built into the training.

coaches.name: Willie Chen
coaches.bio: Former New Zealand representative specialising in doubles and mixed. Willie takes a holistic approach — a coaching philosophy focused on every detail on and off the court, including skills, match strategy, strengthening and recovery, and mental and nutrition preparation.
coaches.focus: Intermediate to advanced doubles and mixed players

coaches.name: Alex Zhao
coaches.bio: A Chinese National Level 1 athlete with over ten years of coaching experience. Alex's coaching is not only about improving badminton skills, but about helping players develop resilience, confidence and a strong work ethic — stepping outside their comfort zone, staying focused when training gets hard, and understanding that meaningful progress takes time and consistent effort.
coaches.focus: Intermediate to advanced singles and mixed players

coaches.name: Cici Xie
coaches.bio: A passionate badminton coach focused on developing young athletes through strong technique, tactical awareness and confidence on court.
coaches.focus: Junior high-performance development — singles and doubles technical and tactical coaching, competition preparation

coaches.name: Alfred Wong
coaches.bio: Holds a Badminton New Zealand Level 2 coaching certificate and has been a Canterbury head coach for more than 20 years, developing players who have gone on to compete internationally. He is also one of New Zealand's most successful masters players, winning three national titles at the 2026 NZ Masters National Championships. Alfred brings decades of experience to every session, helping players of all ages build sound technique, stay composed under pressure and play smart, tactical badminton.
coaches.focus: Junior to senior high-performance development — singles and doubles, competition preparation

coaches.name: Elly Li
creds: 2023 NZ U19 National Champion, Women's Singles
coaches.bio: 2023 NZ U19 National Champion in Women's Singles. Elly is passionate about sharing her experience and helping players build their skills, confidence and enjoyment of the game — for her, coaching is as much about growth, discipline and a positive mindset on and off the court as it is about becoming a better badminton player.
coaches.focus: Junior and adult beginners and intermediate players

coaches.name: Kyle Zhang
coaches.bio: Kyle trained competitively in Beijing during his junior years and has coached at BAPN since May 2025. He works with everyone from junior beginners to competitive juniors and adults, with a strong focus on fundamentals, good habits and long-term development — and is just as invested in building players' confidence, perseverance and responsibility on and off the court.

coaches.name: Sean Wong
coaches.bio: Sean believes players improve most when they enjoy the game. His goal is a positive and encouraging environment where every player can build confidence, celebrate their progress and develop at their own pace.

coaches.name: Ken Wong
coaches.bio: Passionate about badminton and about helping players of all levels improve their game. Ken's focus is on building strong fundamentals, patience and a love for the sport.

coaches.name: Uzi (Husnain) Idris
coaches.bio: Uzi helps players elevate their game through tailored technique training, agility drills and match strategy. Let's smash your goals together.

programs.name: Junior Tier 4 — Foundation
programs.summary: First steps: grip, footwork, balance and the basic strokes, taught through games so young players want to come back.
programs.note: Runs through school terms. Two sessions a week.

programs.name: Junior Tier 3 — Development
programs.summary: For teens starting out or coming back to the game. Sound technique and movement first, then match play.
programs.note: Runs through school terms. Two sessions a week.

programs.name: Junior Tier 2 — Intermediate
programs.summary: Structured technical and tactical work for players competing in school or club events, with regular match play under pressure.
programs.note: Runs through school terms. Two sessions a week.

programs.name: Junior Tier 1 — Elite
programs.summary: The performance tier. Singles and doubles technical and tactical coaching, competition preparation, and sessions with visiting national and international coaches and players.
programs.note: By selection. Runs through school terms, two sessions a week.

programs.name: Adult Tier 2 — Social & Club
programs.summary: Coached group training for adults who want to actually improve — technique, movement and match play in a social setting.
programs.note: Runs through school terms. One session a week. UCanBC members: $230 per term.

programs.name: Adult Tier 1 — Advanced & Representative
programs.summary: High-intensity squad training for competitive adults — tactical doubles and singles work, conditioning and tournament preparation.
programs.note: By selection. Runs through school terms, one session a week.

programs.name: Holiday Camp
programs.summary: A full week of coaching in the school holidays — skills, games and tournament play, with partner workshops on recovery and nutrition. One booking covers every day.
programs.note: First or second week of each school holiday. Enrolments close the Monday before the camp, or when it's full.

programs.name: Saturday Social Club
programs.summary: Open play every Saturday night. Turn up, pay on the night, get a game.

news.title: BAPN players and coaches shine at the NZ Masters National Championships
news.excerpt: Coach Alfred Wong led the way with three national titles, with Mitch Hejl and Catherine Nguyen also winning gold and head coach Cici Xie reaching a final.
body: BAPN players and coaches came home from the NZ Masters National Championships 2026 with a haul of titles — a proud moment for the whole academy.

BAPN coach Alfred Wong led the way with three titles: Men's Singles 50+, Men's Doubles 40+ and Men's Doubles 45+. Winning in both singles and doubles across more than one age group at a national event is a remarkable achievement.
Mitch Hejl won the Women's Singles 55+ title, and Catherine Nguyen won the Division 2 Mixed Doubles. BAPN head coach Cici Xie reached the final of the Women's Doubles 35+.
Ann Lee, Anna Ritche and Slava Sirotov also represented BAPN at the championships, and every one of them did the academy proud.
The results show that at BAPN, badminton isn't just for juniors. Adult players train with the same structure and high standards — and it shows when it counts.

news.title: Elsa and Rohan dominate the 2026 Otago U17 Championships
news.excerpt: Two BAPN juniors finished on the podium in every event they entered — two titles for Elsa, a title and a third for Rohan, and silver together in the mixed.
body: BAPN juniors Elsa Meng and Rohan Gala had an outstanding weekend at the 2026 Otago U17 Championships, finishing on the podium in every event they entered.
Elsa won both the Girls' Singles and the Girls' Doubles. Rohan won the Boys' Doubles and took third place in the Boys' Singles. The pair also teamed up in the Mixed Doubles and finished second.

Results like these come from hours of work on court, and both players have earned every one of them. To celebrate, BAPN's retail partner My Badminton Shop gave Elsa and Rohan each a gift to mark their success.

news.title: BAPN juniors step onto the national pathway
news.excerpt: Marco Sun and Katrina Huang selected for the Badminton New Zealand U15 Development Squad, and Ray Gao invited to the U15 National Camp.
body: Three BAPN juniors have been recognised at national level this year.

Marco Sun and Katrina Huang were selected for the 2026 Badminton New Zealand U15 Development Squad. The squad brings together young players from across the country who show the skill, work ethic and potential to go further in the sport.

Ray Gao was invited to the 2026 U15 National Camp after a strong 2025 season, which included a Top 8 finish in Division 1 at the AIMS Games, one of the country's biggest intermediate-age sporting events.
This is exactly what BAPN's development pathway is built for: strong foundations first, then the support to take the next step when a player is ready. Congratulations, Marco, Katrina and Ray!

news.title: Rangi Ruru takes gold at the South Island Secondary Schools Championships
news.excerpt: With weekly coaching and tournament support from BAPN, Rangi Ruru's team won back-to-back gold.
body: BAPN is proud to be the coaching partner of Rangi Ruru Girls' High School's badminton programme, and the partnership has already paid off.

With weekly coaching and tournament support from BAPN, Rangi Ruru's team won back-to-back gold at the South Island Secondary Schools Championships. It was a great result for the players and their school, and a reminder of how much school badminton can grow with the right support.
BAPN is committed to giving back to the community and helping grow the sport in Canterbury schools, and we look forward to seeing Rangi Ruru go even further.
